subject.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` tool, and if so should it be implemented as a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted `agentTurn` with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: This changes core model-facing scheduling behavior and crosses session-state, cron delivery, interruption, restart, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API and security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that resumes the caller session, proves interruption/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep existing cron and yield surfaces
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and leave delayed work to cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` where their ownership is already documented.

options.title: Narrow to an extension seam
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point instead of a default core tool if maintainers want optional scheduling outside the standard tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require a revised implementation that resumes the caller session, proves interruption/restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron session-target and live probe history makes this the strongest routing owner for the product/API choice.
